raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Preserve the reusable head of CPU-offloaded prefixes while their requests are still running, across store batches and KV groups. Related to [the unfinished-request observation in #58804](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58804#issuecomment-6098736505); this addresses that eviction pattern rather than the issue's entire throughput regression.

## Claims

- Positioned keys share a provisional request rank, with later token positions evicted first across batches.
- `insert(key, chunk, req_context)` assigns new chunks their final provisional rank directly. First observations still handle resident prefixes reused by load/store and anchor requests before allocation retries.
- Finalization commits recency and ARC frequency accounting; transfer pinning, newer shared accesses, reset and keys without positions retain their behavior.

## Validation

Latest review revision: Linux x86_64, Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cpu, based on the bot-merged head `b27bfdfde95e835043749b82bc3d4e2c558eace0`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/base.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/lru.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/arc.py vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/test_factory.py docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md
```

76 manager/policy tests and 500 tiering/scheduler tests passed. All applicable hooks passed. The two new insertion-contract cases fail on the merged head because `insert` lacks `req_context`; with the revision, ready and pending chunks both evict tail before head without a follow-up access call. The original running-prefix regression tests previously gave 11 failed/2 passed against the unmodified base.

A native CPU replay through `LLM` used a two-layer tiny Llama, dummy weights, float32, greedy decoding, two 192-token prompts, block size 32 and eight offload slots. A remains unfinished while B adds pressure. Aborting A, clearing only model-side prefix caching and replaying A gives the same result before and after this interface revision: 64 cached tokens, 2 actual CPU KV blocks loaded and output token IDs `[11, 11, 11, 11]`. A test-only worker synchronously copies real CPU KV pages; the installed native extensions are shared by both runs. This validates usable KV reuse and observed output, not model quality or CUDA transfer behavior.

Manager-only timings, five runs per row, nine groups and batches of eight; median [min,max] milliseconds:

| Chunks/group | Merged PR head | Insertion revision |
|---|---:|---:|
| 64 | 1.980 [1.805,3.454] | 1.807 [1.732,2.703] |
| 256 | 8.911 [7.935,13.120] | 7.887 [7.435,12.620] |
| 1024 | 39.069 [37.165,362.716] | 34.581 [33.813,321.299] |

These are bookkeeping measurements; GPU TTFT and serving throughput were not measured in this review revision.

## Details

Insertion previously made an unfinished request's head older than its tail until finalization. Evicting the head makes every remaining suffix unreachable by contiguous-prefix lookup.

LRU uses `(request_rank, -token_position)` and the existing lazy heap update/compaction paths. The request rank is anchored at first observation; new chunks receive it inside `insert`, while existing resident accesses preserve any newer shared recency. This avoids revisiting the full prefix after every store batch. Cache reset invalidates provisional state. Chunks remain evictable and finalization still commits recency.

Custom `CachePolicy` implementations must accept the additional `req_context` insertion argument; policies that do not use it can ignore it. The custom-policy guide and ARC implementation reflect that interface. ARC frequency promotion remains at finalization.

The fix is distinct from optional in-flight pin protection (#57813), session-aware policies (#50422), GPU-local reuse recording (#57746) and KVCR recency changes (#60469); those target different policies or access sources. This revision addresses the existing review request on #61050.

Thanks for picking this up. I ran it on the Qwen/DFlash workload from my #58804 comment, which the description lists as unmeasured: it brings back the second-turn reuse that 0.31.0 loses there, with no chunk 0 evicted.

Setup: a native RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (GDN + attention, DFlash drafter, 9 KV-cache groups), vLLM 0.31.0 with an out-of-tree patch series (on the offload path it only adds a boot-time warning and a device-pointer translation that adds 0 on native Linux), `--kv-offloading-size 8`, two ~60K-token conversations in flight at once, then each conversation's second turn. The PR cherry-picks onto 0.31.0 without conflicts (the series leaves those three files as upstream ships them). One boot per row:

| | turn 2 cached | read back from CPU |
|---|---|---|
| 0.30.0 | 57,664 and 57,664 (96.3%) | 2.16 GB |
| 0.31.0 | 0 and 0 | 0 |
| 0.31.0 + this PR | 50,880 of 59,718 (85.2%) and 49,184 of 59,887 (82.1%) | 1.90 GB |

With the PR the tier evicts 120 chunks, tail-first within each request, none of them a chunk 0; on 0.31.0 the first victims are chunk 0 of all nine groups.

I had also tried re-ranking a running request's whole observed prefix after each of its store batches. On this workload that gives the same counts to the token and the same victims, so your cheaper bookkeeping costs nothing in hits here. This workload does not exercise the cross-request order, though: at each eviction burst only one request had evictable chunks, so the shared provisional rank had nothing to choose between. That reading comes from the victim list, not from a run built to test it.

Unit, on the same 0.31.0 tree, CPU only: `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies` give 73 passed with the PR, including a test of mine that stores a positioned four-chunk prefix in two batches and expects the tail to go first. Without the PR, those 12 fail (your 11 and mine).

Still unproven: one boot per row and one workload. The rest of the gap to 0.30.0 is tail chunks of every group, attention groups included; for a hybrid model a windowed group's chunks inside the hit would be better victims, but that needs each group's window, so it is a separate change.

This was measured and written with AI assistance (Claude); every number above comes from our own runs.

files.patch:
@@ -188,6 +188,11 @@ Implement `CachePolicy` (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies/base.py`) in your own
 }
 ```
 
+Custom policies must implement `insert(self, key, chunk, req_context)`. The request
+context provides each key's token position through `get_offload_key_position(key)`
+so a policy can establish prefix ordering during insertion. Policies that do not
+use request-specific insertion ordering can accept and ignore `req_context`.
+
 `eviction_policy` is checked against the built-in registry first; if it isn't a registered name, vLLM imports `cache_policy_module_path` and looks up `eviction_policy` as a class name in that module — the same fallback `spec_module_path` provides for a custom `OffloadingSpec`. No import or registration call needs to run before the server starts.
 
 ### Registering a friendly short name (in-process only)

@@ -23,7 +23,9 @@ def __init__(self, cache_capacity: int) -> None:
     def get(self, key: OffloadKey) -> ChunkStatus | None:
         return None
 
-    def insert(self, key: OffloadKey, chunk: ChunkStatus) -> None:
+    def insert(
+        self, key: OffloadKey, chunk: ChunkStatus, req_context: ReqContext
+    ) -> None:
         pass
 
     def remove(self, key: OffloadKey) -> None:

@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@
 from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.common import CPULoadStoreSpec, CPUOffloadingMetrics
 from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.manager import CPUOffloadingManager
 from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.policies.arc import ARCCachePolicy
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.policies.base import ChunkStatus
 from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.policies.lru import LRUCachePolicy
 
 
@@ -1593,3 +1594,181 @@ def test_request_key_positions_order_tails_across_kv_groups():
     output = manager.prepare_store(to_keys([10, 11]), make_req_context("evict"))
     assert output is not None
     assert set(output.evicted_keys) == {group_0_tail, group_1_tail}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("batch_size", [1, 2, 3])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reverse_completion", [False, True])
+def test_unfinished_lru_prefix_survives_pressure_across_store_batches(
+    batch_size, reverse_completion
+):
+    """Keep a contiguous prefix while its owner is still generating."""
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=8)
+    ctx = make_req_context("unfinished")
+    groups = [
+        [make_offload_key(str(position).encode(), group) for position in range(3)]
+        for group in range(2)
+    ]
+    batches = []
+    for start in range(0, 3, batch_size):
+        batch = [key for group in groups for key in group[start : start + batch_size]]
+        for group in groups:
+            for position in range(start, min(start + batch_size, 3)):
+                ctx.set_offload_key_position(group[position], (position + 1) * 16)
+        assert manager.prepare_store(batch, ctx) is not None
+        batches.append(batch)
+        if not reverse_completion:
+            manager.complete_store(batch, ctx)
+    if reverse_completion:
+        for batch in reversed(batches):
+            manager.complete_store(batch, ctx)
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store(to_keys([10, 11, 12, 13]), make_req_context("B"))
+    assert output is not None
+    assert set(output.evicted_keys) == {group[-1] for group in groups}
+    for group in groups:
+        assert all(manager.lookup(key, ctx) is LookupResult.HIT for key in group[:-1])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reuse_method", ["load", "store"])
+def test_unfinished_lru_reused_prefix_outlives_new_tail(reuse_method):
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=4)
+    head, middle, tail = to_keys([1, 2, 3])
+    seed = make_req_context("seed")
+    assert manager.prepare_store([head, middle], seed) is not None
+    manager.complete_store([head, middle], seed)
+    manager.on_request_finished(seed)
+
+    ctx = make_req_context("reuse")
+    for position, key in enumerate([head, middle, tail], 1):
+        ctx.set_offload_key_position(key, position * 16)
+    if reuse_method == "load":
+        manager.prepare_load([head, middle], ctx)
+        manager.complete_load([middle, head], ctx)
+    else:
+        assert manager.prepare_store([head, middle], ctx) is not None
+    assert manager.prepare_store([tail], ctx) is not None
+    manager.complete_store([tail], ctx)
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store(to_keys([10, 11, 12]), make_req_context("B"))
+    assert output is not None
+    assert set(output.evicted_keys) == {middle, tail}
+    assert manager.lookup(head, ctx) is LookupResult.HIT
+
+
+def test_unfinished_lru_backfill_orders_by_token_position():
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=3)
+    ctx = make_req_context("backfill")
+    head, middle, tail = to_keys([1, 2, 3])
+    for position, key in enumerate([head, middle, tail], 1):
+        ctx.set_offload_key_position(key, position * 16)
+    for key in [head, tail, middle]:
+        assert manager.prepare_store([key], ctx) is not None
+        manager.complete_store([key], ctx)
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store([to_key(4)], make_req_context("B"))
+    assert output is not None
+    assert output.evicted_keys == [tail]
+
+
+def test_lru_failed_store_retry_preserves_prefix_order():
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=2)
+    ctx = make_req_context("retry")
+    head, tail = to_keys([1, 2])
+    ctx.set_offload_key_position(head, 16)
+    ctx.set_offload_key_position(tail, 32)
+    assert manager.prepare_store([head], ctx) is not None
+    manager.complete_store([head], ctx, success=False)
+    for key in [head, tail]:
+        assert manager.prepare_store([key], ctx) is not None
+        manager.complete_store([key], ctx)
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store([to_key(3)], make_req_context("B"))
+    assert output is not None
+    assert output.evicted_keys == [tail]
+
+
+def test_lru_reset_discards_unfinished_request_recency():
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=2)
+    ctx = make_req_context("resumed")
+    head = to_key(1)
+    ctx.set_offload_key_position(head, 16)
+    assert manager.prepare_store([head], ctx) is not None
+    manager.complete_store([head], ctx)
+    manager.reset_cache()
+
+    other = make_req_context("other")
+    other_key = to_key(9)
+    other.set_offload_key_position(other_key, 16)
+    assert manager.prepare_store([other_key], other) is not None
+    manager.complete_store([other_key], other)
+    assert manager.prepare_store([head], ctx) is not None
+    manager.complete_store([head], ctx)
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store([to_key(10)], make_req_context("B"))
+    assert output is not None
+    assert output.evicted_keys == [other_key]
+
+
+def test_older_lru_request_does_not_demote_a_newer_shared_access():
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=3)
+    old = make_req_context("old")
+    pinned, cold, shared = to_keys([1, 2, 3])
+    for context, key, position in [
+        (old, pinned, 16),
+        (make_req_context("cold"), cold, 16),
+        (make_req_context("newer"), shared, 32),
+    ]:
+        context.set_offload_key_position(key, position)
+        assert manager.prepare_store([key], context) is not None
+        manager.complete_store([key], context)
+    manager.prepare_load([pinned], old)
+
+    old.set_offload_key_position(shared, 32)
+    manager.prepare_load([shared], old)
+    manager.complete_load([shared], old)
+    output = manager.prepare_store([to_key(4)], make_req_context("pressure"))
+    assert output is not None
+    assert output.evicted_keys == [cold]
+    manager.complete_load([pinned], old)
+
+
+def test_lru_incremental_stores_do_not_rescan_the_prefix():
+    class CountingContext(ReqContext):
+        position_lookups = 0
+
+        def get_offload_key_position(self, key: OffloadKey) -> int | None:
+            self.position_lookups += 1
+            return super().get_offload_key_position(key)
+
+    keys = to_keys(list(range(64)))
+    manager = make_cpu_manager(num_chunks=len(keys))
+    ctx = CountingContext(req_id="incremental")
+    for position, key in enumerate(keys, 1):
+        ctx.set_offload_key_position(key, position * 16)
+        assert manager.prepare_store([key], ctx) is not None
+        manager.complete_store([key], ctx)
+
+    assert 0 < ctx.position_lookups <= 3 * len(keys)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ready_on_insert", [False, True])
+def test_lru_insert_orders_positioned_chunks_without_followup_access(ready_on_insert):
+    """Insertion alone orders new chunks, including out-of-order backfills."""
+    policy = LRUCachePolicy(cache_capacity=3)
+    ctx = make_req_context("insert")
+    head, middle, tail = to_keys([1, 2, 3])
+    for position, key in enumerate([head, middle, tail], 1):

🚀

Thanks for picking this up. I ran it on the Qwen/DFlash workload from my #58804 comment, which the description lists as unmeasured: it brings back the second-turn reuse that 0.31.0 loses there, with no chunk 0 evicted.

Setup: a native RTX 3090, Qwen3.8-27B W4A16 (GDN + attention, DFlash drafter, 9 KV-cache groups), vLLM 0.31.0 with an out-of-tree patch series (on the offload path it only adds a boot-time warning and a device-pointer translation that adds 0 on native Linux), `--kv-offloading-size 8`, two ~60K-token conversations in flight at once, then each conversation's second turn. The PR cherry-picks onto 0.31.0 without conflicts (the series leaves those three files as upstream ships them). One boot per row:

| | turn 2 cached | read back from CPU |
|---|---|---|
| 0.30.0 | 57,664 and 57,664 (96.3%) | 2.16 GB |
| 0.31.0 | 0 and 0 | 0 |
| 0.31.0 + this PR | 50,880 of 59,718 (85.2%) and 49,184 of 59,887 (82.1%) | 1.90 GB |

With the PR the tier evicts 120 chunks, tail-first within each request, none of them a chunk 0; on 0.31.0 the first victims are chunk 0 of all nine groups.

I had also tried re-ranking a running request's whole observed prefix after each of its store batches. On this workload that gives the same counts to the token and the same victims, so your cheaper bookkeeping costs nothing in hits here. This workload does not exercise the cross-request order, though: at each eviction burst only one request had evictable chunks, so the shared provisional rank had nothing to choose between. That reading comes from the victim list, not from a run built to test it.

Unit, on the same 0.31.0 tree, CPU only: `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_manager.py` and `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/policies` give 73 passed with the PR, including a test of mine that stores a positioned four-chunk prefix in two batches and expects the tail to go first. Without the PR, those 12 fail (your 11 and mine).

Still unproven: one boot per row and one workload. The rest of the gap to 0.30.0 is tail chunks of every group, attention groups included; for a hybrid model a windowed group's chunks inside the hit would be better victims, but that needs each group's window, so it is a separate change.

This was measured and written with AI assistance (Claude); every number above comes from our own runs.
